translation.literal: Endowed with faces ruddy, crimson and rose like the young sun, a girl, Speech, red-bodied in the morning, dwelling on earth, whose nature is happiness, of rajas; bearing the fearlessness gesture, the water-pot, the lotus and rosary and the ladle — the Gāyatrī, riding the swan, bringer into being, in the form of Śrī Brahmā, I worship in the heart.
translation.readable: In the morning I worship in my heart the Gāyatrī as a girl, red-bodied, her faces glowing like the rising sun: she is Speech, she dwells on the earth, her nature is happiness; she shows the gesture of fearlessness and holds a water-pot, a lotus, a rosary and the ladle; she rides the swan, brings things into being, and has the form of Brahmā.

meaning: The morning form of the goddess of the Gāyatrī in the Mylapore prayoga. At dawn she is a young girl, red like the rising sun, Speech herself, with the attributes of Brahmā the creator: the water-pot, the rosary, the ladle of sacrifice, the swan as her mount. She is the first of the three: Brahmā’s form and creation at dawn, Rudra’s form and dissolution at midday, Viṣṇu’s form and preservation at dusk.
in_the_rite: Step dhyāna of the Gāyatrī japa, morning service only (the Mylapore prayoga), after the general verse muktā-vidruma.

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Śārdūlavikrīḍita metre, written as two lines. Only M has the verse.

flags.text: M prints मुखैः युक्तां unjoined inside the first pāda; the padaccheda rejoins into मुखैर्युक्तां. Proposed text: बालार्कारुण-शोण-पाटल-मुखैर्युक्तां …

रासजीम् is probably राजसीम् (the morning’s guṇa, beside tāmasī and sāttvikī in the other two verses), and ब्रुवम् probably स्रुवम् (the ladle, Brahmā’s attribute). No second witness has the verse; the text is analysed as M prints it.
